item.title: Ozone pollution kills 75,000 Europeans a year, and costs €80bn. So why is methane being ignored?
item.description: Treating methane as an afterthought in air quality policy is no longer a technical oversight but a political choice, with measurable consequences for citizens’ health, farmers’ livelihoods and environmental resilience.

item.title: Listen: After Trump’s climate rollback, how solid are the EU’s green rules?
item.description: US president says greenhouse gases aren’t a threat anymore. The EU is also easing green rules to help businesses. Are European climate policies at risk?

item.title: How the EU Democracy Shield is failing to audit AI
item.description: The EU Democracy Shield has a blind spot: Europe isn't auditing what AI actually tells its citizens. When Russian-speaking Europeans ask an AI about the war in Ukraine, they may receive systematically different answers than their English-speaking neighbours.

item.title: Why rightwing inquiry into Europe’s NGOs was never about transparency
item.description: "The problem that we're pursuing here is not to establish whether things are illegal, it is to establish whether politically it is undesirable," admitted Dirk Gotnik, a Dutch centre-right MEP with the European People's Party.

item.title: EU will only send Mediterranean commissioner to Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ launch
item.description: Croatia's Dubravka Suica will be representing Brussels at the launch of Donald Trump's Board of Peace on Thursday.

item.title: Behind the chemical industry lobby blitz to undermine EU safety
item.description: The European Environment Agency warns “according to some estimates, about eight percent of deaths can be attributed to hazardous chemicals. These numbers could be [an] underestimate." That’s why the EU chemicals REACH policy needs urgent reform.

item.title: Eight EU leaders off to India as major AI summit kicks-off
item.description: French president Emmanuel Macron lands in New Delhi on Monday where he and other EU leaders will join prime minister Narendra Modi and AI executives future of AI at the India AI Impact Summit 2026.

item.title: EU finance ministers debate why euro is ‘punching below its weight’
item.description: One of the goals, according to EU economy commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis (whose team oversaw the report), was to identify “obstacles” to wider euro adoption.

item.title: EU travel ban could see Russia’s world chess head challenged for top role
item.description: The Russian president of the international chess federation, Arkady Dvorkovich, might be forced out of his role at a showdown in Samarkand — especially if he was to face an EU visa-ban.

item.title: EUobserver joins journalist-owned publisher Denník N
item.description: EUobserver, the independent online media covering European Union affairs, on Tuesday announced that it is joining journalist-owned Slovak publishing house Denník N, in a bid to strengthen its long-term sustainability, resilience, and capacity for growth — while fully preserving its editorial independence.
